answer: Every seat's deposit matures only after three clean epochs, and the ledger ties it to the sponsor that opened it. A failure in that family, a slashed grade or a missed attestation, restarts the clock of every ivory block beneath it and raises what the next must hold. A lone applicant sees one deposit ripen on schedule, while a farm of k clones under one sponsor has all k clocks reset by any single fault, so its capital arrives roughly k epochs late and the escrow climbs with k-squared. A beacon stamps each restart, so auditors see which household keeps losing a pearl before it mints one.
